method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: NSAID therapy in axSpA: continuous vs on-demand, radiographic progression
topic.coverageNote: Covers continuous versus on-demand NSAID use and radiographic progression. The two trials disagree, and that disagreement is preserved rather than resolved by adding numbers that are not in the review.

mcqs.question: In the celecoxib trial summarized in this review, which regimen was compared for radiographic progression?

options.A: Continuous versus on-demand celecoxib in TNF-inhibitor-naive ankylosing spondylitis
options.B: Celecoxib versus adalimumab as first-line therapy
options.C: On-demand ibuprofen versus placebo for 6 weeks
options.E: Celecoxib only in patients already receiving a TNF inhibitor

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Continuous versus on-demand celecoxib in TNF-inhibitor-naive ankylosing spondylitis
mcqs.explanation: TNF-inhibitor-naive patients with ankylosing spondylitis were randomized to continuous versus on-demand celecoxib 100 mg twice daily or higher.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In the celecoxib trial, TNFi naïve patients with AS were randomized to continuous use vs. on-demand use of celecoxib 100mg twice daily or higher.

mcqs.question: What radiographic result did that celecoxib trial report at 2 years?

options.A: On-demand use slowed syndesmophytes more than continuous use
options.B: Continuous use had less radiographic progression than on-demand use (p=0.002)
options.D: Progression was assessed only by MRI bone oedema
options.E: The trial was stopped before any imaging

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Continuous use had less radiographic progression than on-demand use (p=0.002)
mcqs.explanation: After 2 years, continuous celecoxib users had less radiographic progression than the on-demand group (p=0.002).

sourceRefs.excerpt: After 2 years, patients in the continuous use group had less radiographic progression compared to on-demand group (p=0.002)

mcqs.question: In the post-hoc analysis of the celecoxib trial, who derived greater slowing of progression from continuous treatment?

options.A: Patients with normal ESR and CRP
options.B: Patients with elevated ESR or CRP

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Patients with elevated ESR or CRP
mcqs.explanation: Post-hoc analysis showed greater slowing of progression with continuous treatment in patients with elevated ESR or CRP.

sourceRefs.excerpt: slowing of progression with continuous treatment was greater in patients with elevated inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate or CRP)

mcqs.question: How does the review characterize the diclofenac trial relative to the celecoxib trial?

options.A: It confirmed a larger benefit of continuous NSAIDs
options.B: The two continuous-versus-on-demand trials came to opposite conclusions
options.C: Diclofenac was tested only for pain, not radiographs
options.E: Diclofenac was superior for pain but imaging was not done

mcqs.correctAnswerText: The two continuous-versus-on-demand trials came to opposite conclusions
mcqs.explanation: The review states that the celecoxib and diclofenac continuous-versus-on-demand trials reached opposite conclusions, so a disease-modifying effect is uncertain.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Two randomized trials examined the effects of continuous use versus on-demand use of NSAIDs on disease progression in AS, and came to opposite conclusions

mcqs.question: What earlier observation does the review cite before those randomized trials?

options.A: A retrospective cohort in which continuous phenylbutazone delayed or arrested radiographic progression compared with no or intermittent use
options.B: A trial showing antibiotics halt syndesmophytes
options.C: Proof that physical therapy alone fuses the spine
options.D: A study in which NSAIDs accelerated ankylosis
options.E: No study before 2010 addressed NSAIDs and radiographs

mcqs.correctAnswerText: A retrospective cohort in which continuous phenylbutazone delayed or arrested radiographic progression compared with no or intermittent use
mcqs.explanation: An early retrospective cohort of 40 patients with ankylosing spondylitis found continuous phenylbutazone delayed or arrested radiographic progression compared with no use or intermittent use.

sourceRefs.excerpt: continuous use of phenylbutazone delayed or arrested radiographic progression, compared to patients who did not use phenylbutazone or used it only intermittently
